name: Core Scientific
hq: Dover, DE (registered); Austin, TX operating hub
founded: 2017; Chapter 11 December 2022 → emerged and relisted January 2024
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Core Scientific is the shareholder-revolt vindication story of the AI-landlord cohort — nine months after stockholders voted down CoreWeave's $9B all-stock acquisition (October 30, 2025), the company signed AMD as a second 500 MW-class anchor (July 28, 2026: ~530 MW across five sites, >$14B potential base contracted revenue, expandable to 2.5 GW, AMD taking warrants for 30M shares at $23.47), doubling contracted capacity to ~1.1 GW and total backlog past $24B. The CoreWeave book (~590 MW, $10.2B over 12-year take-or-pay terms) is meanwhile delivering ~200 MW ahead of schedule — >430 MW billing by mid-July 2026 at a ~$635M annualized run-rate. Derived economics say the rejection paid: the AMD book prices ~$1.76M per MW-year vs ~$1.44M for CoreWeave. BACKGROUND: Founded 2017; the 2022 bitcoin crash put it through Chapter 11 (emerged January 2024, $400M of debt equitized); the emergence warrants (CORZW $6.81 / CORZZ $0.01) now whipsaw GAAP results — a $1.05B non-cash warrant charge produced a $1.16B 'loss' in Q2 2026 in the same quarter revenue beat consensus by 20% (the first revenue beat in over four quarters, per Zacks). A February 2026 restatement (FY2024–Q3 2025 non-reliance; demolition-committed mining assets improperly kept capitalized) knocked the stock 14%. Stockholders' deficit -$2.4B; $3.3B of 7.75% secured notes fund the buildout; self-mining (15.7 EH/s at YE2025) is winding down site by site.
ecosystemRole: We assess Core Scientific as the miner-pivot cohort's most instructive case in tenant credit and capital-markets dynamics: the first landlord with two distinct 500 MW-class anchors (a leveraged neocloud and a chip vendor building a hosting channel against NVIDIA's ecosystem), the cleanest proof that rejecting an anchor-tenant acquisition can precede better economics, and — via the AMD warrants — another instance of silicon vendors buying equity in their infrastructure chain. For power-chain vendors: 50–200+ kW/cabinet high-density colocation with direct liquid cooling, a stated $11–12M/MW build cost (~40% of it long-lead OFE — transformers, switchgear, generators, chillers), the Muskogee and Pecos campuses each expanding toward 1.5 GW gross with behind-the-meter solutions, and >600 MW of leasable power added by acquisition in 2026 alone (Polaris DS ~$444M, Hunt County $233M). Basis: company decks and filings, trade coverage; ~2.5 GW total leasable potential with AMD.

productsAndServices.name: High-density colocation (HDC) — the core business
productsAndServices.description: Single-tenant, build-to-suit high-density colocation for AI workloads: 50–200+ kW per cabinet, 30 MW+ contiguous blocks, direct liquid cooling, distributed- or block-redundant power designed for five-nines availability, lithium-ion UPS, carrier-neutral fiber. Sold through a nine-step integrated platform (site → utility → power → fiber → design → long-lead procurement → construction → 24/7 operation → expansion) across 10+ data centers in 7 states (~1.4 GW gross utility power at YE2025).
highlights: ~1.1 GW customer-contracted power; $24B+ contracted revenue; ~$1.8B average annualized colocation GAAP revenue potential
Colocation revenue ramp: $31.3M (Q4 25) → $77.5M (Q1 26) → $136.7M (Q2 26) at 59% segment gross margin
Build cost $11–12M/MW (excl. $1–2M/MW tenant fit-out); ~45% construction labor, ~40% owner-furnished equipment
productsAndServices.positioning: First miner-convert with two 500 MW-class anchor tenants; deliveries ran ~200 MW ahead of plan by mid-2026 — the execution record is the sales pitch ('Value is not announced. It is delivered.' — CEO Sullivan).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: 12–15-year take-or-pay leases with annual escalators; customer-funded fit-out credited against hosting fees; project-level financing (the $3.3B notes sit against five datacenter subsidiaries with CoreWeave revenue in a lockbox).
targetSegments: Chip vendors building hosting channels (AMD + an unnamed AMD-credit-backed neocloud)
productsAndServices.roadmap: AMD deliveries: Pecos & Auburn 1H 2027, Dalton & Muskogee 2H 2027, Hunt County 1H 2028 — full ~530 MW by end-2028; >2 GW additional pipeline under due diligence for 2028–2030.

productsAndServices.name: The CoreWeave book (anchor #1)
productsAndServices.description: ~590 MW of critical IT across six sites (Denton ~260, Dalton ~175, Muskogee ~70, Marble ~65, Austin ~20 MW) under 12-year take-or-pay contracts totaling $10.2B (~$850M average annual revenue at 80–85% anticipated margin). CoreWeave funds up to $1.5M/MW of build-out, credited back against ≤50% of monthly hosting fees. Buildout 'substantially complete': >430 MW billing as of mid-July 2026; Dalton finishes early 2027.
highlights: CoreWeave = 100% of colocation revenue until AMD deliveries begin (per the FY2025 10-K risk factor) — ~83% of total Q2 2026 revenue
Relationship began 2019 with GPU hosting for mining; survived a rejected $5.75/share cash bid (2024) and the failed $9B merger (2025) with contracts unaffected
productsAndServices.positioning: The concentration the AMD deal exists to dilute: post-AMD, CoreWeave is ~42% of backlog — still the only revenue until 2027.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Take-or-pay with UCC liens on data-center infrastructure (excluding GPUs); no unilateral termination.
targetSegments: CoreWeave (which sublets to its own hyperscaler/AI-lab customers)

productsAndServices.name: The AMD partnership (anchor #2, July 2026)
productsAndServices.description: Strategic partnership deploying AMD Instinct GPUs, EPYC CPUs, and ROCm software on dedicated capacity: ~530 MW across five sites (Pecos ~185, Dalton ~120, Hunt ~110, Muskogee ~82, Auburn ~32 MW) — 377–380 MW leased by AMD directly plus ~150 MW through an unnamed AMD-credit-backed neocloud. >$14B potential base contracted revenue over ~15 years with 2.5%/yr escalators; expansion potential to 2.5 GW; AMD receives market-priced warrants for 30M shares at $23.47 (~9.3% if exercised).
highlights: Derived rate ~$1.76M/MW-year — ~20%+ richer than the CoreWeave book
Trade press framing: AMD building a hosting channel to counter NVIDIA's neocloud ecosystem — silicon vendors now compete through landlords
productsAndServices.positioning: The vindication asset: signed nine months after shareholders rejected the CoreWeave merger, it alone approaches the entire rejected $9B deal value in contracted revenue.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term take-or-pay leases; revenue begins with 2027 deliveries.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Initial delivery early 2027; full 530 MW by end-2028; 2.5 GW expansion optionality.

productsAndServices.name: Bitcoin self-mining & hosted mining (winding down)
productsAndServices.description: Self-mining: ~135,500 miners / 15.7 EH/s at YE2025, shrinking as sites convert to HDC — revenue fell from $408.7M (FY2024) to $229.2M (FY2025) to $21.5M in Q2 2026; $208M of bitcoin sold in Q1 2026 to fund the AI buildout. Hosted mining: winding down — the 10-K states the company 'may not derive consequential' hosting revenue going forward.
highlights: Down to ~2 mining sites by end-2026; Pecos' 300 MW of mining power is the next conversion
Proprietary fleet-management software 'capable of managing 1 million miners' — a legacy asset
productsAndServices.positioning: The most explicit treasury-liquidation approach in the cohort: BTC is sold to pour concrete.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Self-mining for own account; residual third-party hosting.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Remaining sites repurposed for HDC 'as circumstances allow' (company framing).

recentDevelopments.headline: Completes ~$444M cash acquisition of Polaris DS LLC — ~440 MW of gross grid-connected power (Oklahoma Gas & Electric) advancing Muskogee toward 1.5 GW gross / ~1.0 GW leasable; >600 MW of leasable power added YTD by acquisition
recentDevelopments.read: Buying energized grid capacity outright is now cheaper than queuing for it — ~$1M per gross MW for the connection alone.

recentDevelopments.headline: AMD partnership: ~530 MW across five sites, >$14B potential base contracted revenue, up to 2.5 GW expansion; AMD takes warrants for 30M shares at $23.47; ~150 MW of it routed through an unnamed AMD-credit-backed neocloud
recentDevelopments.read: The second anchor, at richer per-MW economics than the first — and AMD's answer to NVIDIA's neocloud ecosystem, fought through landlords. The unnamed neocloud tenant is a standing disclosure gap.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q2 2026: revenue $164.2M beat Zacks consensus by 20.4% (first revenue beat in 4+ quarters); colocation $136.7M at 59% gross margin; GAAP net loss $1.16B on a ~$1.05B warrant fair-value charge as the stock rallied
recentDevelopments.read: The crossover print: colocation is now 83% of revenue, adjusted EPS turned positive — and GAAP simultaneously showed the biggest 'loss' in company history, purely from its own share price rising against the emergence warrants.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q1 2026: 243 MW billing (~$350M annualized colocation revenue); Hunt County, TX (~430 MW, approved ERCOT interconnection) acquired for $233M; Muskogee and Pecos 1.5 GW expansion plans detailed; gross power pipeline 4.5 GW
recentDevelopments.read: The pipeline machine restarted post-merger-distraction — two Texas/Oklahoma campuses each targeting a gigawatt of leasable power.

recentDevelopments.headline: $3.3B of 7.75% senior secured notes due 2031 priced at 99.25 via Core Scientific Finance I LLC — secured by five datacenter subsidiaries, CoreWeave revenues paid into a lockbox; Morgan Stanley/J.P. Morgan strategic facilities expanded to $1B earlier in March
recentDevelopments.read: Project-style leverage on a company two years out of Chapter 11 — the market financed the standalone plan the shareholders voted for.

recentDevelopments.headline: Restatement: FY2024 10-K and three 2025 10-Qs deemed non-reliable — mining assets committed for demolition (site conversions) were improperly kept capitalized; 10-K/A and 10-Q/As filed same day; stock fell 14.4%
recentDevelopments.read: A conversion-accounting failure unique to the miner-pivot trade: the faster you demolish mining halls for AI, the more impairment discipline matters. The audit-committee chair had left the board months earlier.

recentDevelopments.headline: Stockholders vote down the $9B all-stock CoreWeave merger (0.1235 ratio, no collar); agreement terminated same day; CoreWeave rules out a re-bid; commercial contracts unaffected
recentDevelopments.read: A landmark of AI-infrastructure governance: Two Seas Capital's campaign (backed by ISS and Glass Lewis) argued the uncollared CRWV ratio passed all the volatility to CORZ holders while peers tripled — the market's first successful revolt against anchor-tenant absorption.

recentDevelopments.headline: CoreWeave agrees to acquire Core Scientific for ~$9.0B all-stock (~$20.40/share implied, 66% premium) — after a rejected $5.75/share cash bid in June 2024 and a bidding escalation from 0.092 to 0.1235 exchange ratio
recentDevelopments.read: The offer history itself (cash $5.75 → ~$20.40 in 13 months) is the cleanest mark-to-market of what AI-ready power became worth.

recentDevelopments.headline: Denton expansion (+70 MW, ~$1.2B) completes the CoreWeave book: ~590 MW across six sites, $10.2B cumulative 12-year contracted revenue
recentDevelopments.read: The contract stack that made everything else possible — assembled in nine months of 2024 option exercises from an initial 16 MW Austin pilot.

recentDevelopments.headline: Emerges from Chapter 11 with $400M of debt equitized; relists on Nasdaq the next day with tranche warrants (CORZW $6.81 / CORZZ $0.01) that will dominate GAAP optics for years
recentDevelopments.read: The reset that created today's cap table — and the warrant liabilities ($2.0B at mid-2026) that make reported earnings unreadable without adjustment.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess the shareholder rejection has been vindicated on customer economics, though not yet fully on share price. Basis: the AMD book prices ~$1.76M/MW-year vs ~$1.44M for the CoreWeave book (derived from disclosed totals), total backlog went $10.2B → $24B+ in nine months, and CORZ became the first miner-convert with two 500 MW-class anchors — while the stock, at ~$17.81, sits below the $20.40 implied deal price it rejected. Yahoo's framing is the fair one: 'proven right about customer appeal, not yet about value.'

(High confidence) We assess GAAP results are structurally unreadable and the market has learned to ignore them. Basis: Chapter 11 emergence warrants produce nine-figure non-cash swings in whichever direction the stock moved ($910M charge Q2 2025, $330M gain Q4 2025, $1.05B charge Q2 2026); Zacks and MarketBeat literally disagree on which quarters beat. Colocation revenue, billing MW, and segment gross margin are the readable lines.

(High confidence) We assess the concentration bridge to 2027 is the nearest-term risk. Basis: the 10-K states CoreWeave is 100% of colocation revenue, ~83% of total Q2 2026 revenue; AMD revenue starts only with early-2027 deliveries; mining revenue is being deliberately liquidated ($208M of BTC sold in Q1 2026 alone). Two-plus quarters where one leveraged neocloud's execution is effectively the whole P&L.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the balance sheet is the bet shareholders implicitly made: releverage a post-bankruptcy company to build the standalone plan. Basis: $3.3B 7.75% secured notes + $1.085B converts against a -$2.4B stockholders' deficit, $11–12M/MW build costs implying ~$6B for the AMD program, and $677M of 2026 site acquisitions — against $1.8B of liquidity and customer-funded fit-out. The model works if both anchors pay to term; the 2022 bankruptcy is the reminder of what happens when a cycle turns mid-buildout.

(Moderate confidence) We assess governance remains the discount factor. Basis: the February 2026 restatement (with the audit chair's earlier exit), a single-bidder merger process both proxy advisors condemned, two consecutive XMS Capital alumni as CEO and CFO, and warrant/CVR structures only a bankruptcy court could love. The board refresh (Steve Smith of Zayo/ex-Equinix, Mark Adams of Penguin Solutions, 2026) is the counter-signal. Collection gap: no securities litigation tied to the restatement has surfaced, and the Q3 2026 earnings date (est. Oct 23) is not company-confirmed.
